# Summary

This Quarto html vignette and provides example R code for: 1) accessing data from SacPAS (Central Valley Prediction and Assessment of Salmon; [cbr.washintgon.edu/sacramento/](https://cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/)) via custom query urls, and 2) generating figures using these data. We start with simple examples and progress to slightly more complex figures and integrated data sets. We focus on data on River Conditions ([cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/query_river_graph.html](https://cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/query_river_graph.html)) and Fishes ([cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/query_sampling_graph.html](https://cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/query_sampling_graph.html)). The custom query urls can be copied from the SacPAS query tools by clickling the option and submitting the query:

![](images/image_check_mark_query_url.png){fig-alt="Screenshot of a SacPAS query tool section with the \"Submit Query\" button, \"Reset\" button, and checkmark option for \"Generate query url\"." fig-align="center"}

R code blocks in this Quarto html vignette also provide examples of query url strings that can be further customized.

# River Conditions

## Daily Data in one year

```{r}
#| label: river-temp-single-year
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-folding: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# Choose year and site, and create custom query url
year <- "2025"
site <- "KWK"
temp_unit <- "F" # or could be "C"
my_url <- paste0("https://cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/php/rpt/mg.php?sc=1&mgconfig=river&outputFormat=csvSingle&hafilter=All&year%5B%5D=", year, "&loc%5B%5D=", site, "&data%5B%5D=WaterTemperature&tempUnit=", temp_unit, "&startdate=1%2F1&enddate=12%2F31&avgyear=0&consolidate=1&grid=1&y1min=&y1max=&y2min=&y2max=&size=large&resolution=medium")

# Download the data
river_temp_data <- readr::read_csv(my_url)

# Read and save data notes
print(generate_note <- as.character(
  river_temp_data[(nrow(river_temp_data)-1),1]))
print(citation_note <- as.character(
  river_temp_data[(nrow(river_temp_data)),1]))

# Remove the Notes from data set
river_temp_data <- head(river_temp_data, -3)

# Data wrangling
# Date
river_temp_data <- river_temp_data |>
  mutate(date = ymd(str_c(year, `mm-dd`, sep = "-")))
  


# Plot the data
if(temp_unit == "F") {
  ggplot(river_temp_data, aes(x = date, y = value)) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.75) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 1) + 
    labs(
      title = paste("Daily river temperature at", site, "in", year),
      x = "Date",
      y = expression(paste("River temperature (", degree, "F)"))
    ) 
} else {
  ggplot(river_temp_data, aes(x = date, y = value)) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.75) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 1) + 
    labs(
      title = paste("Daily river temperature at", site, "in", year),
      x = "Date",
      y = expression(paste("River temperature (", degree, "C)"))
    ) 
}


```

## Start and End Dates

```{r}
#| label: river-temp-start-end-dates
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: false

# Choose year and site, and create custom query url
year <- "2025"
site <- "KWK"
start_date <- "4%2F1"
end_date <- "10%2F31"
my_url <- paste0("https://cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/php/rpt/mg.php?sc=1&mgconfig=river&outputFormat=csvSingle&hafilter=All&year%5B%5D=", year, "&loc%5B%5D=", site, "&data%5B%5D=WaterTemperature&tempUnit=F&startdate=", start_date, "&enddate=", end_date, "&avgyear=0&consolidate=1&grid=1&y1min=&y1max=&y2min=&y2max=&size=large&resolution=medium")

# Download the data
river_temp_data <- readr::read_csv(my_url)

# Remove the Notes from data set
river_temp_data <- head(river_temp_data, -3)

# Data wrangling
# Date
river_temp_data <- river_temp_data |>
  mutate(date = ymd(str_c(year, `mm-dd`, sep = "-")))

# Plot the data
ggplot(river_temp_data, aes(x = date, y = value)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 1) + 
  labs(
    title = paste("Daily river temperature at", site, "in", year, "from April 1st to October 31st"),
    x = "Date",
    y = expression(paste("River temperature (", degree, "F)"))
  )

```

## Multiple years (with legend)

```{r}
#| label: river-temp-multiple-years-legend
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: false

# Pull in data for years 2024, 2025, and 2026 
year <- "2024"
site <- "KWK"
my_url_2024 <- paste0("https://cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/php/rpt/mg.php?sc=1&mgconfig=river&outputFormat=csvSingle&hafilter=All&year%5B%5D=", year, "&loc%5B%5D=", site, "&data%5B%5D=WaterTemperature&tempUnit=F&startdate=1%2F1&enddate=12%2F31&avgyear=0&consolidate=1&grid=1&y1min=&y1max=&y2min=&y2max=&size=large&resolution=medium")

year <- "2025"
site <- "KWK"
my_url_2025 <- paste0("https://cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/php/rpt/mg.php?sc=1&mgconfig=river&outputFormat=csvSingle&hafilter=All&year%5B%5D=", year, "&loc%5B%5D=", site, "&data%5B%5D=WaterTemperature&tempUnit=F&startdate=1%2F1&enddate=12%2F31&avgyear=0&consolidate=1&grid=1&y1min=&y1max=&y2min=&y2max=&size=large&resolution=medium")

year <- "2026"
site <- "KWK"
my_url_2026 <- paste0("https://cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/php/rpt/mg.php?sc=1&mgconfig=river&outputFormat=csvSingle&hafilter=All&year%5B%5D=", year, "&loc%5B%5D=", site, "&data%5B%5D=WaterTemperature&tempUnit=F&startdate=1%2F1&enddate=12%2F31&avgyear=0&consolidate=1&grid=1&y1min=&y1max=&y2min=&y2max=&size=large&resolution=medium")

# Data-cleaning function
prepare_data <- function(my_url) {
  river_temp_data <- readr::read_csv(my_url)
  river_temp_data <- head(river_temp_data, -3)
  river_temp_data <- river_temp_data |>
    mutate(date = ymd(str_c(2000, `mm-dd`, sep = "-")))
  river_temp_data
}

# Clean the data from each query call
river_temp_data_2024 <- prepare_data(my_url_2024)
river_temp_data_2025 <- prepare_data(my_url_2025)
river_temp_data_2026 <- prepare_data(my_url_2026)

# Combine rows into a single data frame
river_temp_data <- bind_rows(river_temp_data_2024, river_temp_data_2025, river_temp_data_2026)

# Plot the data
ggplot(river_temp_data, aes(x = date, y = value, color = factor(year))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  labs(
    title = paste("Daily river temperature at", site, "from 2024-2026"),
    x = "Month",
    y = expression(paste("River temperature (", degree, "F)")),
    color = "Year"
  )

```

# Fish Data

## Rotary Screw Trap

```{r}
#| label: fish-rst
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: false

# Pull in data for years 2024, 2025, and 2026 
year <- "2026"
location <- "UBC"
isCumulative <- 0 # 0 for non-cumulative data, 1 for cumulative data
non_cumulative_url <- paste0("https://www.cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/php/rpt/sampling_graph.php?sc=1&outputFormat=csv&year=", year, "&species=CHN%3AWinter&loc=trap%3A", location, "%3A0&cumData=", isCumulative, "&typeData=raw&resolution=medium")
print(non_cumulative_url)

year <- "2026"
location <- "UBC"
isCumulative <- 1 # 0 for non-cumulative data, 1 for cumulative data
cumulative_url <- paste0("https://www.cbr.washington.edu/sacramento/data/php/rpt/sampling_graph.php?sc=1&outputFormat=csv&year=", year, "&species=CHN%3AWinter&loc=trap%3A", location, "%3A0&cumData=", isCumulative, "&typeData=raw&resolution=medium")

# Data-cleaning function
prepare_data <- function(my_url, isCumulative) {
  data <- readr::read_csv(my_url)
  data <- head(data, -7)
  data <- rename(data, count = 2)
  data <- data |>
    mutate(
      date = ymd(Date),
      isCumulative = isCumulative
    )
  data
}

# Clean the data from each query call
non_cumulative_data <- prepare_data(non_cumulative_url, 0)
cumulative_data <- prepare_data(cumulative_url, 1)

# Combine rows into a single data frame
upper_battle_creek_data <- bind_rows(non_cumulative_data, cumulative_data)

# Plot the data
ggplot(upper_battle_creek_data, aes(
    x = date,
    y = count,
    color = factor(isCumulative, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Non-cumulative", "Cumulative"))
  )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %d", date_breaks = "1 week", date_minor_breaks = "1 day") +
  labs(
    title = paste("Winter Chinook, Upper Battle Creek RST"),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Raw catch",
    color = NULL
  )


```
